propositions: A git fetch that establishes a connection but transfers zero bytes hangs for the full 300s wall-clock timeout instead of aborting on throughput starvation within seconds.

The fix adds http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime git config options (1000 B/s over 10s by default) to detect and abort byte-starved connections, but must not abort legitimately slow but progressing transfers.

Transient low-speed aborts are retried in-process a bounded number of times (3 attempts × 10s = ~30s worst case) to self-heal within the same review, while non-low-speed failures (auth, bad ref) are not retried.

Module size constraint forces a code split: git-subprocess and fetch-locking plumbing moves from repo_snapshot.py (788 LOC, at 800 cap) into new sibling git_fetch.py, keeping one-directional dependency and unchanged public surface.
